audit.why: 6/10 difficulty is fair, though the 55.06% win rate is the strongest of Sion's lanes in this slice — the lane is straightforward once Grievous Wounds is respected.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Warwick Levels 2, 3, first item and 2+ items, and split 4-5 and 6 as Skill. Every why on the page argues the opposite: whys[1] says the level-2 exchange is Sion's, whys[2] calls level 3 'his entire lane pattern undone', mid calls 4-5 'your cruising window' and level 6 'swings decisively in your favor'. The packet chart reads Skill/Sion/Sion/Sion/Sion/Sion/Skill.
audit.why: A 55% win rate with the owner's prose claiming six favourable stages cannot coexist with a chart handing four of them to the enemy.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill, Sion, Sion, Sion, Sion, Sion, Skill in both layers with ratings inverted to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three kit errors. (a) 'He has no dash to escape the stun' — Jaws of the Beast is a lunge and carries the dash flag. (b) W-shield was quoted at an 8-second cooldown; it is 15/14/13/12/11. (c) Infinite Duress was described only as a suppress; it is a CHANNEL, so it can be cancelled outright by Decimating Smash or Unstoppable Onslaught, which is the single most valuable fact in this matchup and appeared nowhere.
audit.why: Cancelling the ultimate turns his best all-in into a 110-second cooldown he gets nothing for.
audit.corrected: Dash corrected, real W cooldown written, channel-cancel written into spikes[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's scaling logic ran backwards. whys[5], spikes[2] and late all argued that stacking HP makes Warwick's sustain irrelevant. Jaws of the Beast deals damage based on the TARGET's maximum health and heals him for damage dealt, so every point of Heartsteel HP makes his bite hit harder and heal him more.
audit.why: This told the user to buy the exact stat that feeds the enemy, and to skip the item that actually answers him.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around percent-max-health scaling with Grievous Wounds as the answer instead of raw HP or armour.

edits.before: Charged Q knockup into E armor-shred is his entire lane pattern undone — he has no dash to escape the stun and the shred amplifies every subsequent hit.
edits.after: Charged Q knockup into E armor-shred undoes his lane pattern — Jaws of the Beast is his only lunge on an 8s cooldown, so once he spends it he cannot leave the stun.

edits.before: His only spike here is on-hit pressure, and your W-shield on an 8-second cooldown resets his trades every engagement — deny extended brawls and you win every exchange.
edits.after: His only spike here is on-hit pressure, and your W-shield is 13s at rank 3 — trade on that timer, not on his, and deny the extended brawl where his passive regen takes over.

edits.before: Heartsteel stacking compounds your HP passive from kills and assists; Warwick's Q heal is a flat percent of damage dealt, not a percent of your HP, so the bigger you get the less his sustain matters.
edits.after: Heartsteel compounds your HP, but Jaws of the Beast bites a percent of your MAX health and heals him for what it deals — the bigger you get the more it feeds him. Buy Grievous Wounds, not armour.

edits.before: Heartsteel starts stacking your HP passive hard; Warwick's on-hit Q heal cannot keep pace with the HP total you are accumulating every fight.
edits.after: Heartsteel stacks your HP hard — but his bite scales off that same max health, so pair the first item with Bramble Vest or the spike works for him instead.

edits.before: Infinite Duress suppresses you for 1.5 seconds while he heals — never fight him below 50% HP or his W gives him a full movement-speed beacon before the suppress lands.
edits.after: Infinite Duress is a 1.5s suppressing channel — a charged Q or Unstoppable Onslaught cancels it outright — and staying above 50% HP keeps Blood Hunt from beaconing him onto you.

edits.before: Stack Heartsteel to compound your HP passive until his on-hit heal is irrelevant against your total
edits.after: Buy Grievous Wounds before more HP — his bite scales off your max health and heals him for what it deals

edits.before: Late game you are a max-HP wall that Warwick's kit is not designed to crack — his Q heal is percentage-based on the damage it deals, and once you are sitting on 5,000+ HP from Heartsteel and your kill-passive stacks, he simply does not deal enough damage for his sustain to matter. Your zombie passive means even a successful Infinite Duress all-in frequently costs him more than he earns, as he must survive your counter-damage AND a zombie phase after. In teamfights, R-charge to engage and use your enormous HP pool as a frontline; Warwick wants isolated low-HP targets and your team fight presence denies him those windows. Anti-heal (Executioner's Calling component or Thornmail later) shuts his sustain loop entirely if the lane ever gets competitive.
edits.after: Late game you are a max-HP wall, but not one his kit ignores — Jaws of the Beast bites a percent of your MAXIMUM health and heals him for the damage it deals, so every Heartsteel stack makes his bite hit harder and heal him more. Armour is the wrong answer here; Grievous Wounds is, and it belongs in the build before the fight rather than after it. Your zombie passive still means a successful Infinite Duress often costs him more than he earns, since he must survive your counter-damage AND a zombie phase after. In teamfights, R-charge to engage and use your HP pool as a frontline; Warwick wants isolated low-HP targets and your presence denies him those windows. Stay above 50% and Blood Hunt never lights up.

notes: The percent-max-health finding is the important one here: three separate fields told the user that stacking HP makes Warwick's sustain irrelevant, when Jaws of the Beast scales off the target's max health. Sion Q's listed range of 10000 is a data artifact and was not used. Packet 'games' disagrees with itself (626 at top level, 583 inside packet) — reporting, not editing.
